mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of FEDFUNDS-tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes despite the consumption decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 3 consecutive months by >1% each month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decrease in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.25 percentage points indicates a coordinated monetary easing and disinflation, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both fall by >=0.25% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically higher than baseline in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) of at least 0.5% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both rise by >=0.5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decrease in the unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher discount rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below 1.2 million units for six consecutive months signals a prolonged housing downturn, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly below zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).
